title: Magnon band splitting without altermagnetism in CuF2
authors: Ioannis Rousochatzakis, Oleg Janson, Alexander A. Tsirlin
abstract: Conclusive identification of an altermagnetic state requires going beyond mere symmetry arguments. We illustrate this in a combined computational and experimental study of the rutile-like material CuF$_2$, which is on the list of predicted altermagnets. Using ab initio and linear spin-wave calculations supplied by magnetization measurements, we show that CuF$_2$ in its experimental monoclinic structure can be described by a spin-$\frac12$ model of weakly coupled square-lattice layers with the in-plane coupling $J_1\simeq 115$ K and two synergistic antiferromagnetic interplane couplings amounting to 4% and 8% of $J_1$, respectively. Driven by long-range superexchange, these interlayer couplings are oblique to the square planes, resulting in the unit-cell doubling in the magnetically ordered state, thus effectively suppressing any altermagnetic band splitting. Concurrently, we identify unusually strong Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, $|\mathbf D|/J_1\simeq 0.3$, that produce spin canting and, together with order-by-disorder effect, pin the Néel vector to the crystallographic $b$-axis. Additionally, DM anisotropy promotes magnon band splitting, but these bands remain non-chiral. Our results highlight the importance of relativistic effects even in $3d$ magnets with altermagnetic symmetries.
summary: This work investigates the magnetic state of CuF2, a material predicted to be an altermagnet. By combining DFT calculations with spin-wave theory, the authors demonstrate that the material exhibits a conventional antiferromagnetic order, not an altermagnetic one. The study provides detailed quantitative evidence regarding the role of DM interactions and the resulting magnon spectrum.
main_problem: To conclusively determine the magnetic state of CuF2 and rule out the possibility of altermagnetism, moving beyond simple symmetry arguments.
main_result: The magnetic order in CuF2 is confirmed to be antiferromagnetic (AFM), not altermagnetic, due to a doubling of the magnetic unit cell. While DM interactions cause magnon splitting, these bands are non-chiral.
method: The study combines ab initio calculations (DFT/GGA) for electronic structure with linear spin-wave theory and fitting to experimental magnetization data.
model_or_system: The system is CuF2, modeled as a quasi-2D square-lattice antiferromagnet with weak interlayer couplings. The Hamiltonian is refined to include strong Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interactions.
key_observables: Magnon band splitting ($\omega_\pm(k)$), chiral structure factor ($C(q, \omega)$), magnetic susceptibility ($\chi(T)$), and magnetic unit cell doubling.
important_parameters: In-plane coupling $J_1 \simeq 115 	ext{ K}$ and DM anisotropy $|D|/J_1 \simeq 0.3$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on fitting to an effective one-orbital model and assumes the magnetic structure is governed by the observed unit cell doubling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate crystal structures, energy vs. volume curves, and magnon dispersions comparing DM effects in 2D vs. 3D AFM systems.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the stability and basic magnetic structure (AFM vs. Altermagnetic) using DFT, to deriving an effective Hamiltonian incorporating exchange and DM terms, and finally analyzing the resulting magnon spectrum via spin-wave theory.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of magnon dispersion and the explicit calculation of the chiral structure factor provide rigorous theoretical tools for distinguishing between different magnetic ground states in correlated insulators.
